name: xTool M1 Ultra
tagline: Laser + blade cutter in one : unique hybrid for crafters and sticker makers
tldr: The M1 Ultra combines a diode laser with a digital blade cutter (like a Cricut on steroids). Cut vinyl, paper, and fabric with the blade; engrave wood and leather with the laser. Niche but powerful if your workflow mixes both : wrong pick if you only want laser cutting.

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

pros: 10W on xTool M1 Ultra: engraving-first : photo fills and leather at moderate speeds
Software listed on the profile : test your workflow (LightBurn or maker app) on scrap first
cons: Clear cast acrylic and thick production cutting still favor CO₂, not diode power alone
Confirm optical wattage on the listing before you buy
beginnerNotes: This profile covers xTool M1 Ultra. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks before buying, then compare nearby models on the Compare page.
proTips: Use blade for all vinyl and paper : laser charred edges on paper look amateur. Use laser for wood/leather personalization. Rotary add-on expands tumbler work on the laser module.
primaryUse: Hybrid craft machine for vinyl stickers, paper goods, and light laser personalization in one workflow.

faq.question: Is M1 Ultra a laser cutter?
faq.answer: Partially. The laser module is 10W diode : fine for engraving and thin cuts, not for acrylic sign production. The blade cutter is the differentiator for vinyl and paper.

faq.question: M1 Ultra vs Cricut + separate laser?
faq.answer: M1 Ultra saves space and one software stack. Separate machines give you a stronger laser (D1 Pro) plus a dedicated Cricut. Choose integrated convenience vs best-in-class laser.

mainObjective: Vinyl & paper cutting plus light laser engraving in one machine

images.alt: xTool M1 Ultra laser engraver : xTool

editorialDepth.advantages: xTool M1 Ultra 10W suits makers who sell marks, photos, and gifts more than daily panel cutting. Reasonable open-frame entry price.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if you already quote 4 mm+ cutting in production. Not for cast acrylic or bare metal without spray.
